title: install.v1: the plugin install file, install.json
description: The file '$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/recursion/plugins/install.json' as the daemon reads it today (core/recursion_core/daemon/plugins.py, read_install): this install's trusted developer keys, the grants its user made, the destinations and credential names reserved for effect owners, and the installer's key for the authority ledger. Version 1 is today's format with nothing added, so a file written to this schema is read by today's daemon; it has no version field because today's reader refuses a field it does not know. Every top-level field may be left out; a missing file means no trusted key and no grant, so nothing gets a permission. The file is owner-only and is written by the install commands, never by a plugin. A grant is bound to one artifact digest and one signing key: a grant for another digest or key grants nothing. Two rules the reader enforces cannot be written in a schema: no two grants name the same plugin_id; and the file must be a regular file of the operator's that no one else can write.

trusted_keys.description: This install's own trusted developer keys: a label for each, and the Ed25519 public key as 64 lower-case hex digits. 'Signed' means signed by one of these.

reserved.description: Network destinations and credential-name prefixes that an effect owner reserves: no grant may name one.

authority_anchor.description: The installer's public key for the authority ledger, or null when none is configured.

key_id.description: A public key's stable id: 'ed25519:' and the first 32 hex digits of the key's SHA-256.

grant.description: What the user granted one plugin. signer_key_id is the key the grant is bound to, or null for a manual grant to an unsigned plugin. unsigned_order_acknowledged records that the user granted 'order' to an unsigned plugin behind the warning. order_after_revoked_key and order_after_revocation_generation record that the user turned 'order' back on after that key was revoked, at that generation of the revoked-key list.

permissions.description: The seven permissions today's reader takes (plugin_security/manifest.py, PERMISSIONS). The five names that are new in the version 1 manifest are NOT here: today's reader refuses a grant that lists one (daemon/plugins.py, read_install), so a file that granted one would not be read by today's daemon. Granting them needs the reader to change first; when it does, this list grows and this schema says so.
